caveat: Every value below is an assumption, not a live figure. The calculator stamps this version onto shared results so a stale number is visible rather than silently wrong.

trip.petrolNote: Sinopec with card ~$2.66 · Shell full price ~$3.46
trip.fuelNote: A typical Singapore sedan does about 12.

alternatives.fareNote: Check the SMRT or bus app for the exact fare — we don't estimate it. Cross-island averages around $1.80.

grabEstimate.caveat: Ignores surge, time of day and platform fees. No public Grab API exists, so this stays an estimate and is always labelled as one.

speeds.grabWaitNote: Assumption, not data. grabBufferMin is a typical wait for the car; grabWaitWorstMin is a bad-day wait (rain, peak). Arrive-by plans use the worst case so a Grab plan is never the one that makes you late.
speeds.caveat: H3 and H4. No traffic model, no transfer or platform-wait model. The MRT figure is the most under-modelled number in the build.
speeds.note: Times are for the whole return journey, matching the costs, which are all return figures too. The drive buffer is time spent finding a space; the Grab buffer is time spent waiting for the car.

verdict.caveat: H7. A flat $5 band is arbitrary and does not scale with trip cost. A proportional band, max(5, 0.15 x driveTotal), is the noted fix path but is deliberately NOT implemented here, because D9 in the handoff specifies the flat threshold.

limits.caveat: Guards against absurd input. Singapore is about 50 km end to end, so 300 km of one-way driving is already generous.

habits.caveat: Owner decision 2026-10-20. Band edges are assumptions, Singapore time. A pattern is shown only when at least minSame of the last window trips in the same situation went the same way. Shown, never applied to the verdict (show-only).
